item.title: Correlated quantum criticality and topological magnetoelectric response in Bi2Se3
item.description: arXiv:2611.03670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A defining feature of quantum materials is that multiple orders govern low-energy physics and are not independent. We study Bi$_2$Se$_3$ by combining DFT with a renormalized correlated honeycomb model in which frustrated magnetic order and helical topological surface states are coupled via one control parameter. The surface states map to a honeycomb Hubbard model with frustrated $J_1$--$J_2$ exchange. Exact diagonalization up to 20 sites shows the N\'{e}el structure factor and valence-bond-solid order parameter cross at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.22$, agreeing with QMC/DMRG, and a dynamical spin structure factor broadens near the crossover, as expected for a spinon continuum. Band inversion of the renormalized tight-binding model occurs on the same critical locus, producing jumps in the Chern number and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant mirrored by the skyrmion charge $Q$. This gives a microscopic link: $Q$ selects the axion angle and thus the topological magnetoelectric coupling. We distinguish axion coupling, independent of skyrmion helicity, from the helicity-dependent magnetoelectric multipole coupling, whose toroidal component scales as $\sin\gamma$ and vanishes for N\'{e}el-type textures. We derive the $Q$-topological magnetoelectric energy and estimate $\sim 10^{-20}\,\mathrm{J}$ per skyrmion per cycle for few-tesla fields. The cycle is thermodynamically bounded: constant-$\theta$ cycles extract no net work, and efficiency is limited by axionic entropy change.
item.dc:creator: Aniekan Magnus Ukpong

item.title: Thermal Phase Transition of Three Dimensional Orthogonal Metals
item.description: arXiv:2611.03804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthogonal metals provide a paradigmatic example of strongly entangled metallic states whose transport and thermodynamic properties resemble those of conventional Fermi liquids, while their single-electron excitations remain fundamentally distinct. Despite considerable interest in their unusual ground-state properties, orthogonal metals in three spatial dimensions and their finite-temperature behavior remain relatively unexplored. Here, we investigate a three-dimensional orthogonal metal and characterize the thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures associated with its finite-temperature phase transition. Starting from a simple model of fermions coupled to spin degrees of freedom, we perturbatively demonstrate that the thermal transition known to occur in the purely bosonic limit persists in the presence of coupling to a gapless Fermi surface. We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes. In particular, we calculate the evolution of the physical-electron spectral function and identify characteristic signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find a pronounced contrast in low-energy spectral weight between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes without requiring conventional symmetry-breaking order. Our results establish finite-temperature orthogonal-metal physics as a possible mechanism for pseudogap-like behavior in three-dimensional and quasi-two-dimensional layered materials with non-negligible interlayer hopping, which may be applied to the recent experiments in $\mathrm{Sr_2 VO_3 Fe As}$.
item.dc:creator: Inho Song, Minsu Park, Hanbit Oh, Eun-Gook Moon

item.title: Collective Modes of Fractional States Beyond Landau Levels
item.description: arXiv:2611.03805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collective modes provide a powerful probe into the properties and stability of topologically ordered and strongly interacting phases of matter, such as fractional quantum Hall states. Yet, the description of fractional-state excitations away from the Landau-level limit remains a formidable challenge. We develop a framework for describing collective excitations in the strong-coupling regime of coupled-wire constructions and show that they emerge as solitons and breathers of effective sine-Gordon theories. This approach provides a systematic route to studying collective modes in a broad class of fractional states. Applied to a coupled-wire construction of the fractional quantum Hall effect, the framework captures key features of the magnetoroton branch. It naturally extends to fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating that magnetoroton-like collective modes persist well beyond the Landau-level limit. We find that the magnetoroton gap increases as the Fubini-Study metric approaches the ideal (trace-condition) limit, highlighting the important role of quantum geometry in the stability of fractionalized phases and their collective excitations. The same trend favors the stability of the long-wavelength quadrupolar mode associated with the chiral graviton. Together, these results identify a distinct interplay between fractionalization and quantum geometry, and provide an analytical framework for studies of collective excitations in fractional topological matter.
item.dc:creator: Peleg Emanuel, Yuval Oreg

item.title: Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, Yb$_y$Co$_3$G$e_{3-x}$Sn$_x$
item.description: arXiv:2611.03822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong electron correlations and topology offer complementary routes to controlling electrical conduction, as correlations can make electrons heavy (e.g. Kondo lattices) whereas topology can make them behave as massless particles (e.g. Dirac or Weyl systems), and having both in one material is rare. In Kondo lattice systems, Kondo hybridization between localized 4$f$ and conduction electrons strongly enhances the quasiparticle mass, where in Weyl-Kondo systems these Kondo-renormalized bands form Weyl states, and simultaneous signs of both Kondo and Weyl states in one material have not been observed in transport. Here we report signs of both in the kagome metal \ce{Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x} by combining magnetotransport, heat capacity, magnetization, angle-resolved and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, and DFT+U calculations to reveal Yb-dependent Kondo scattering developing into lattice coherence, with extrapolated Sommerfeld coefficient of approximately 2 ~Jmol$_{\mathrm{Yb}}^{-1}$K$^{-2}$. Transverse magnetoresistance (MR) follows single-ion Kondo scaling, whereas longitudinal transport contains an additional negative response proportional to B$^2$ and remains unsaturated up to 32 T, consistent with a chiral anomaly. These findings support a picture of Kondo and Weyl-like conduction arising from distinct electronic states without external Fermi-level tuning, suggesting a possible route to combining correlated and topological functionality in a bulk material.
item.dc:creator: M. P. Dubbelman, R. Meduri, T. M. Kyrk, Z. Cheng, P. Maderson, D. Pizzirani, A. Das, V. N. Vreede, X. Liu, N. Witt, S. Grytsiuk, C. M. Polley, M. R\"osner, A. Grubi\v{s}i\'c-\v{C}abo, S. Bhattacharyya, R. E. Baumbach, M. E. Kamminga, S. Wiedmann, J. Y. Chan, M. N. Ali

item.title: Repulsion-Driven Topological Superconductivity in Twisted MoTe$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.03833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a microscopic model of twisted MoTe$_2$ with screened Coulomb interactions produces topological superconductivity. Using the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) on infinite cylinders, we find that the narrow Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ has Cooper pair correlations that strengthen with cylinder circumference, consistent with two dimensional superconductivity. The superconductor has chiral $f$-wave pairing around the valley center, and its topology produces chiral Majorana edge modes and non-Abelian vortex cores. At zero displacement field, the superconductor spans fillings $-0.78\lesssim\nu\lesssim-0.72$, close to the experimental range, and extends in a dome to finite displacement field. We then predict how its stiffness evolves with the filling and the tunable displacement field. The interplay with screening length is also examined. Nearby, we find a fractional Chern insulator, a topological charge density wave, a metal, and a charge-ordered state. The last is a candidate for the reentrant integer Hall regime in experiments. These results establish a route from repulsive interactions in microscopic models of moir\'e materials to chiral topological uperconductors with chiral Majorana edge modes.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Wang, Tomohiro Soejima, Norman Y. Yao, Ashvin Vishwanath, Michael P. Zaletel, Taige Wang, Daniel E. Parker

item.title: Korringa factor in Dirac-nodal-line systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.03994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Korringa factor $K(\alpha)$ in the nuclear magnetic resonance studies is a widely used measure of electron-correlation effects in metals and is conventionally interpreted using the non-correlated value $K(\alpha)$ = 1. In Dirac-fermion systems, however, the non-correlated reference value depends on the electronic density of states (DOS) and differs from that of conventional metals. Here, we theoretically investigate the non-correlated Korringa factor $K^*(\alpha)$ in a Dirac nodal-line (DNL) system with finite nodal-line dispersion using a DOS-based approach. We show that $K^*(\alpha)$ exhibits an intrinsic temperature dependence, continuously evolving from the Dirac-fermion value of 1.71 at high temperatures to the metallic value of 1 at low temperatures. The crossover temperature is found to be proportional to the nodal-line dispersion width, identified as the characteristic energy scale governing the non-correlated Korringa factor in DNL systems. We further demonstrate that Landau quantization generates singular DOS structures that strongly enhance $K^*(\alpha)$, producing pronounced peaks even in the absence of electron correlations. In addition, $K^*(\alpha)$ exhibits two distinct types of magnetic oscillations arising from intra-level and inter-level contributions. The latter originates from the overlap of singular points belonging to positive and negative quantum-number Landau subbands at the Fermi level and represents a unique consequence of the finite energy dispersion of a DNL. These results provide a quantitative reference for interpreting NMR experiments in DNL materials and for identifying genuine correlation effects beyond DOS-induced contributions.
item.dc:creator: Takahiko Sekine, Kanoda Kazushi

item.title: Resolving magnetic order and dynamics with polarized neutron scattering: a practical guide to longitudinal polarization analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.04050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutron scattering provides microscopic information on magnetic order and spin dynamics. Most experiments, however, use unpolarized neutrons and do not fully exploit the information carried by the neutron spin. Longitudinal polarization analysis (LPA), established in the pioneering work of Moon, Riste, and Koehler at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the late 1960s, separates magnetic and nonmagnetic scattering contributions through their different effects on the neutron spin. In this review, we illustrate how LPA can distinguish weak magnetic scattering from nonmagnetic contributions, constrain small moment components, and resolve the spin-space anisotropy of magnetic excitations. We introduce the formalism connecting measured polarization channels to magnetic quantities and discuss scattering geometry, crystallographic projections, and corrections for finite polarization. Our aim is to provide a practical guide for neutron scatterers using LPA to determine magnetic structures and characterize spin excitations in quantum materials. We conclude with opportunities in altermagnets, unconventional superconductors, and kagome magnets.
item.dc:creator: Sijie Xu, Pengcheng Dai

item.title: LaQX: A JAX Toolkit for Neural Quantum State Simulations of Lattice Quantum Many-Body Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.04333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural quantum states provide accurate variational representations for interacting lattice fermions and spins. Turning a new ansatz into a reproducible calculation, however, requires coordinated implementations of the Hamiltonian, sampling, optimization, observables, and accelerator parallelism. We present LaQX (Lattice Quantum simulation based on jaX), an open-source neural quantum state library based on JAX that organizes these components through common functional interfaces. Beyond ground-state variational Monte Carlo, LaQX supports excited-state calculations, Green's Function Monte Carlo refinement, adiabatic evolution, and real-time evolution with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo. It consolidates methods developed in recent high-accuracy neural quantum state studies of the Hubbard model and frustrated magnets, and the package has been used to investigate the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model. We document these capabilities with reproducible calculations for Hubbard, $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg, altermagnetic Hubbard, and interacting Hofstadter models. Function-oriented modules separate the scientific components and limit the source context needed for extensions by human developers and large language models. Source code, documentation, and executable examples are available at https://github.com/bytedance/laqx.
item.dc:creator: Yuntian Gu, Chaohui Fan, Ruichen Li, Haoxiang Chen, Weizhong Fu, Yixiao Chen, Dingshun Lv, Weiluo Ren, Tao Xiang, Liwei Wang, Mingpu Qin, Xiang Li

item.title: Why strong spin-orbit coupling does not destabilize the Dirac spin liquid in the Yb delafossites
item.description: arXiv:2611.04607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the U(1) Dirac spin liquid (DSL) of the triangular lattice. Strong spin-orbit coupling gives their exchange an XXZ anisotropy $\Delta$ and bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ that lock the spin frame to the lattice. We show that, within a single layer of a stable Heisenberg DSL, these couplings generate no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator of their own. Inversion at the bond centers removes the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya channel that gaps the kagome DSL, so the locked symmetry forbids a mass, density or current at any order and, assuming continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. Every Lorentz-scalar four-fermion operator induced by spin-orbit coupling shares an SU(4) multiplet, and hence its scaling dimension, with a Heisenberg-allowed one, and the nine non-scalar quartics without such a partner arise only at second order and are irrelevant at large $N$. The Heisenberg DSL itself allows a Lorentz-vector quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, which a stable phase must also render irrelevant. Beyond a single layer, spin-orbit coupling opens an interlayer monopole channel in rhombohedral stacking. If the Heisenberg DSL is instead multicritical, an anisotropy as small as that of KYbSe$_2$ matters only below tens of mK. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, and exact diagonalization indicates that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not yet fix the K-point exponent, and gapless out-of-plane spin fluctuations at the K point would test the chiral-Ising selection.
item.dc:creator: Yasir Iqbal

item.title: Spin-orbit-locked symmetry and the stability of the triangular Dirac spin liquid in the ytterbium delafossites
item.description: arXiv:2611.04608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the triangular U(1) Dirac spin liquid, QED$_3$ with $N_f=4$, but their exchange is spin-orbit coupled. Under their spin-orbit-locked space group we determine which operators the XXZ anisotropy and the bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ induce, and at what order. Symmetry forbids every Dirac mass, density and current at any order and, assuming adiabatic continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. At linear order the couplings reach only spin-2 members of the quartic multiplets $\mathbf{20}'$ and $\mathbf{84}$, which share their dimensions with Heisenberg-allowed operators. At second order $J_{\pm\pm}$ and $J_{z\pm}$ renormalize the anisotropy through $J_{z\pm}^2-2J_{\pm\pm}^2$, and nine spin-1 quartics without Heisenberg partners appear, irrelevant at $O(1/N)$. A single layer of a stable Heisenberg spin liquid thus acquires no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator from spin-orbit coupling. The Heisenberg liquid itself allows a Lorentz-vector $\mathbf{20}'$ quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, with two-loop $\epsilon$-expansion estimates 2.9-3.5. Rhombohedral stacking adds triplet-monopole tunneling between layers at first order. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, with crossover exponent $y_T\simeq0.74$-1, and exact diagonalization shows that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. The out-of-plane spectrum at the K point then stays gapless, and the spin-flip to non-spin-flip ratio grows as $\omega^{-0.56}$ at leading order. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not fix the K-point exponent. In-plane fields induce a chiral mass and an out-of-plane moment proportional to $\sin3\varphi$, zero along the bonds and canceling between CsYbSe$_2$ layers, which the planar thermal Hall effect can test.
item.dc:creator: Yasir Iqbal

item.title: Thermodynamic Evidence for Multiple Field-Induced Phases in an Anisotropic Kagome Antiferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2611.04675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kagome antiferromagnets are predicted to host exotic field-induced phases, yet experimental identification of their thermodynamic signatures remains challenging. Here we combine specific heat ($C$) and ultrasound measurements up to 36 T and down to 0.5 K to map the $H-T$ phase diagram of the anisotropic kagome magnet Y$_3$Cu$_9$(OH)$_{19}$Cl$_8$. We show that the suppression of long-range antiferromagnetic order with field at $\sim 15$ T approximately coincides with the onset of the unconventional $1/6$ (or $1/9$) magnetization plateau previously observed in this system. The attenuation (and sound velocity) then intriguingly increases down to 0.5 K just at $\mu_0H = 15$ T, and $C/T$ becomes temperature independent. Moreover, our measurements are consistent with the opening of a spin gap $\Delta_0\simeq3.5\pm 0.3$ K within the plateau and reveal a further compressible (ungapped) phase beyond the plateau phase, unveiling a rich sequence of field-induced phases in this quantum magnet.
item.dc:creator: M. Schuchard, Q. Barth\'elemy, C. Marcenat, N. Wack, P. Puphal, A. De Muer, D. LeBoeuf, T. Klein

item.title: Small-data physics-informed ML model for magnetic exchange based on chemical composition and structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.04681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we propose an ensemble model based on a swarm of dense neural networks, able to predict Heisenberg exchange interactions within less than 1% error. The model uses the inputs of the ab-initio Schr\"odinger equation, i.e. the compound structure and chemical composition. In this first work, we trained the model on a few compounds of the hexagonal manganite family and were able to infer, with similar accuracy, the J values for other compounds of the same family at randomly chosen geometries, thus showing that we accurately learned the effect of the chemical composition and structure on effective magnetic integrals J.
item.dc:creator: Brice Kengni Zanguim, Thibaut V\'ery, Marie-Bernadette Lepetit

item.title: Closed- and open-system characterization of the Yukawa-SYK model in real time
item.description: arXiv:2611.04704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strongly correlated matter without quasiparticles is central to many-body physics, quantum chaos, and quantum gravity, motivating a considerable effort toward its realization in tabletop experiments. Two challenges remain: laboratory platforms are open systems, so conformal behavior must survive dissipation, and it must be identified through measurable quantities. We address both challenges in the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (YSYK) model, in which bosons and fermions interact as in, e.g., light-matter systems, but through random all-to-all couplings that drive the boson to criticality without fine tuning. Solving the model in real time using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we treat closed and open systems within a unified framework and, in both cases, consider a thermal steady state to map their phase diagrams. In addition to the known conformal and impurity (or SYK$_2$) regimes, we identify novel high-temperature regimes in which the fermions are driven by an essentially bare boson and show that their dynamics is captured by a quadratic model with time-dependent random hopping. Across all regimes, the fermionic softening of the boson is bounded by a ``criticality budget'' determined only by the Yukawa coupling and the temperature. Coupling the boson with a thermal environment induces a mass shift that deforms the boundaries between different regimes and exhausts the criticality budget, thus imposing a bound on temperature and dissipation rate compatible with self-tuned criticality. We further introduce a set of markers built from the two-point functions that separate all identified regimes, are accessible in linear response, and require no fit of the conformal exponents. We complement them with the quantum Fisher information, deriving upper bounds with and without dissipation. These results may help characterize holographic quantum matter beyond the closed setting.
item.dc:creator: Alex Windey, Christian H. Johansen, Philipp Hauke, Andrea Legramandi

item.title: Hidden Triakontadipole Order in the Triangular-Lattice Magnet CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. Experiments have variously suggested a quantum spin liquid, proximate umbrella point, and disorder-suppressed magnetic order. Here we trace these contradictions to an overlooked multipolar degree of freedom: the transverse pseudospin of the $|\pm5/2\rangle$ Kramers doublet is a rank-5 triakontadipole rather than an ordinary dipole. Analyzing the magnetization, neutron spectra, and thermodynamics on equal footing, we establish a dipole-triakontadipole XXZ model with $J_{\perp} \simeq 0.65$ K and $J_c \simeq -0.13$ K. The resulting planar triakontadipolar superfluid order is hidden from dipolar probes, explaining the absence of a magnetic Bragg peak in neutron scattering. The zero-field excitations separate into a low-energy triakontadipole wave and a broad higher-energy continuum. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus open a new avenue for high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Bo Liu, Yuan Gao, Zhen Ma, Shufan Cheng, Xinyang Liu, Jinsheng Wen, Wei Li

item.title: SrMn$_2$Ge$_2$: A metallic system with anomalous magnetotransport properties
item.description: arXiv:2611.04984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The structural, electronic, and physical properties of previously unexplored layered tetragonal compound SrMn$_2$Ge$_2$ are reported. The compound crystallizes in the ThCr$_2$Si$_2$-type structure with a crystallographic parameters $c/a$ ratio of $2.535(3)$, significantly smaller than those of the related BaMn$_2$$Pn_2$ compounds ($Pn =$ P, As, Sb, Bi), indicating enhanced interlayer interaction between the moment-bearing Mn-ions. Magnetic susceptibility measurements suggest an antiferromagnetic ground state with a high Ne\'{e}l temperature $T_{\rm N} > 350$~K\@. A large and positive magnetoresistance (MR) of approximately $50\%$ is observed at low temperatures, which follows a power-law field dependence with exponent $n = 1.50(8)$. Low-temperature electrical resistivity data reveal Kondo-like features. Heat capacity measurements show no signs of a phase transition below 300~K and further confirm a metallic ground state. Electronic structure calculations reveal a three-dimensional Fermi surface and suggest the presence of substantial electronic correlation effects.
item.dc:creator: A. van der Spuy, R. Warmbier, A. M. Strydom, Daniel Wamwangi, Abhishek Pandey

item.title: Evidence for a Dirac Spin Liquid in the Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet from High-Precision Neural-Network Quantum States
item.description: arXiv:2611.05174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet is a central model in the study of quantum spin liquids, yet its ground-state properties remain unresolved. We perform large-scale variational Monte-Carlo calculations using neural-network quantum states (NQSs) with kagome-geometry-aware message-passing convolution on two-dimensional tori containing up to 300 spins, and achieve exceptionally low variational energies for the kagome model. The spin and dimer structure factors show no evidence of magnetic or valence-bond long-range order. Moreover, the dominant symmetry-resolved spin and dimer correlations exhibit a common scaling behavior consistent with the emergent $SO(6)$ monopole multiplet of the Dirac spin liquid. Finally, the fidelity of the optimized NQSs with Gutzwiller-projected mean-field states increasingly favors the Dirac state over the competing $Z_{2}$ candidates as the system size grows. Together, these complementary results provide evidence for a $U(1)$ Dirac spin-liquid ground state in the kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-Hang Sun, Christopher Roth, Ao Chen, Markus Heyl

item.title: Many Electrons, One Determinant: Hartree--Fock Theory, Basis Sets, and Molecular Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2611.03680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This chapter accompanies the lectures on Hartree--Fock theory and on basis sets and molecular integrals at the \href{https://www.esqc.org}{European Summer School of Quantum Chemistry (ESQC) 2026}. Intended for doctoral students, it develops the single-determinant description of electronic structure from antisymmetry and the variational principle to the orbital equations and their finite-basis matrix representation. Detailed derivations connect the energy functional, the Fock operator, excited determinants, and the interpretation of orbital energies. Restricted, unrestricted, and generalized formulations show how the choice of variational space affects spin symmetry, symmetry breaking, and the limitations of the Hartree--Fock approximation. The computational development covers orthogonalization, self-consistent-field iteration, convergence acceleration, overlap-based occupation selection, and orbital analysis, distinguishing orbital stationarity from stability. A connection to second-order M{\o}ller--Plesset perturbation theory explains the correlation-energy expression and the cost of transforming electron-repulsion integrals from atomic to molecular orbitals. The basis-set and integral development examines radial and angular flexibility, contraction, basis-set incompleteness, and superposition error. The Gaussian product theorem leads to one- and two-electron integrals, recurrence relations, integral screening, and low-rank representations. Worked examples and exercises with detailed solutions connect these derivations to practical calculations. Historical perspectives and explicit notation conventions provide context for the approximations and algorithms that underpin molecular electronic-structure theory.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Fran\c{c}ois Loos

item.title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.03817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.
item.dc:creator: Rolando Ramirez Camasca, Xiang Li, Ting-Chun Lin, John McGreevy

item.title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.04015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a scheme to realize Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial bands in the strongly correlated regime of a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and strong Hubbard interaction. Spin-flip hopping suppressed by the large Zeeman detuning is resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, yielding a correlated spin-orbit coupling that depends on the local particle configuration. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning the interaction strength and particle filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold $^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results highlight density-assisted spin-orbit coupling as a mechanism for realizing Weyl superfluidity in strongly correlated systems.
item.dc:creator: Yong-Huan Wang, Shuai Chen, Xin-Chi Zhou

item.title: On the universality of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.04238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The standard definition of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory requires regularizing the entangling surface and factorizing the Hilbert space, which in turn involves a choice of boundary conditions at the regularized surface. This raises two natural questions which are open at present. The first is under what conditions there is a choice of boundary conditions that leads to a unitary map between the original Hilbert space and the factorized one, which is a necessary condition for a well-defined entanglement entropy. The second concerns the situation where there are multiple such choices, in which case the question is whether they all yield the same entropy, or at least the same terms usually referred to as universal. Focusing on topological theories and using three-dimensional Chern-Simons theory as a concrete illustration, we show under specified assumptions that different such choices affect only the non-universal terms in the entropy, such that the remaining terms are universal in this sense as well, while we explicitly demonstrate that boundary conditions corresponding to non-unitary maps can change these terms. We then explain how a similar argument applies to two-dimensional conformal field theories and discuss a condition for universality in general theories.
item.dc:creator: Orr Sela

item.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,\alpha),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,\alpha)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring $F$-matrices.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Harper, Ben-Michael Kohli

item.title: Vertex-resummed kinetic theory of dipole-symmetric bosons from 2PI effective action
item.description: arXiv:2611.04468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The formalism of non-equilibrium dynamics for the dipole-symmetric $U(N)$ model involving $N$-component charged scalar fields is studied on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour by a systematic $1/N$ expansion of two-particle-irreducible (2PI) effective action to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The differential equations describing non-equilibrium evolution equations of two-point functions and field expectation values related to the symmetry breaking in the dynamics are derived, which encompass scatterings between modes essential in the late-time evolution and thermalization beyond the scope of the mean field. At the late-time regime of the evolution, the leading-order (LO) gradient expansion is performed to construct the vertex-resummed kinetic theory by encoding non-perturbative effects in the vertex through the resummation, which is distinct from the standard kinetic theory written by the weak-coupling expansion.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Wei Su

item.title: Intra-unit-cell Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy of the cuprate Bi$_{1.2}$Pb$_{0.8}$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The predominantly $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing symmetry of cuprate superconductors is well established, yet its microscopic manifestation in local Cooper-pair tunneling remains less explored. Here, we investigate Bi$_{1.2}$Pb$_{0.8}$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$, using Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy with a conventional $s$-wave superconducting Pb tip. We observe a zero-bias conductance enhancement whose approximately quadratic dependence on junction conductance is consistent with phase-diffusive Josephson tunneling. Atomic-resolution conductance maps and site-resolved spectra reveal a pronounced intra-unit-cell modulation, with enhanced Josephson response near oxygen sites and strong suppression near copper sites and along diagonal directions. Microscopic calculations incorporating the bilayer electronic structure and realistic Wannier-based tunneling matrix elements reproduce the observed spatial pattern through interference between pairing contributions of opposite signs. Our results reveal how the sign-changing $d$-wave superconducting order parameter manifests itself in atomic-scale Josephson tunneling, providing complementary evidence for unconventional pairing symmetry in cuprates.
item.dc:creator: Fengyu Yao, Jiong Mei, Wenjin Mao, Runxin Li, Yuchen Huo, Miaomiao Wang, Quanxing Wei, Guihao Jia, Qing Qu, Cui Ding, Lin Zhao, Zhuoyu Chen, Ming-Qiang Ren, Kun Jiang, X. J. Zhou, Jin-Feng Jia, Qi-Kun Xue, Yu-Jie Sun

item.title: Nonreciprocal charge transport in quantum materials: From superconductors to magnetic systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nonreciprocal charge transport, where current flows preferentially in one direction, has become a key topic across quantum materials. This review covers some recent progress in bulk crystals, artificial heterostructures, van der Waals systems, high-temperature superconductors, and magnetic materials. The review discusses both intrinsic origins, such as band-structure effects, and extrinsic ones, including vortex motion, device geometry, and heating artifacts. A central focus is the superconducting diode effect due to its application potential, which shows different critical currents for opposite directions. The review also examines how symmetry breaking, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic order contribute to the observed responses. However, there remain challenges when many exciting findings lack a unified picture, and the field continues to debate the relative importance of various mechanisms. The review highlights key open questions and suggests future directions, including better experimental standards and device integration. This review aims to give a balanced view of what is known, what is uncertain, and where the field might go next.
item.dc:creator: Boning Yu, Yalei Huang, Alltrin Dhanarajagopal, Xiaofeng Xu

item.title: Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2611.04996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

item.title: Hecke Relations from Self-Duality
item.description: arXiv:2611.05002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hecke operators can be used to relate characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges, but it has remained a mystery how to interpret these relations physically. We offer a simple explanation in terms of self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds. Self-dual orbifolds also give more general identities beyond the familiar Harvey-Wu construction, which we illustrate through examples.
item.dc:creator: Justin Kaidi

item.title: Efficient simulations of spectra and transport for multiorbital quantum impurities
item.description: arXiv:2611.05185v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum impurity calculations become challenging when multiple correlated orbitals are treated explicitly, particularly in nonequilibrium steady states. We introduce Coupled-Cluster Coupled Lindblad (C$^3$L), a deterministic approach that combines the recently developed coupled-Lindblad compact bath representation with coupled-cluster theory to compute steady states and Green's functions directly in imaginary and real frequency. C$^3$L has favorable polynomial computational complexity and avoids the sign problem of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). In a real-time multiorbital benchmark, it agrees closely with state-of-the-art QMC while reducing computational cost by four to five orders of magnitude, with a further 10--100-fold speedup on a GPU. Beyond the practical reach of established real-time QMC solvers, four-orbital nonequilibrium impurities with general interactions and biased reservoirs become accessible with C$^3$L. We obtain resonance-resolved transport signatures relevant to scanning tunneling microscopy experiments on molecular junctions.
item.dc:creator: Hao-En Li, Zhen Huang, Lin Lin

item.title: Exact Rokhsar-Kivelson points hosting first-order phase transitions in $S=1$ compass models
item.description: arXiv:2611.05326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study $S=1$ compass models on the square and kagome lattices with bond-dependent bilinear and biquadratic interactions parametrized by an angle $\theta$. For compatible geometries, we determine the exact ground-state manifolds throughout the interval $\pi/4\leq\theta\leq3\pi/4$. At each endpoint, a product of on-site unitaries maps the Hamiltonian to the Laplacian of a configuration graph $\mathcal{G}$ in the $S=1$ Cartesian basis. These endpoints are exact Rokhsar-Kivelson (RK) points, with one ground state per dynamically connected component of $\mathcal{G}$. Each such state is an equal-amplitude superposition in the transformed basis and acquires configuration-dependent phases upon transforming back to the original basis. Both models possess $m=O(L)$ independent and mutually commuting conserved $\mathbb{Z}_2$ line charges, where $L$ is the linear system size, forcing a ground-state degeneracy of at least $2^m$ at the RK endpoints. Throughout the interior region, $\pi/4<\theta<3\pi/4$, the ground-state manifold on each lattice is instead spanned by two product states, both annihilated by the Hamiltonian. On both lattices, each RK endpoint also hosts a first-order transition into this intervening interior phase spanned by the two product states with long-range order.
item.dc:creator: Jay Pandey

item.title: An Exact QFT/Lattice Map for Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice. Unlike domain wall fermions, truncating the local Hilbert space introduces no extra massless modes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval converges as the truncation is removed. The lattice local algebras are of type I and lie between the type III continuum algebras of nested spatial regions, in accordance with the split property. We demonstrate this construction explicitly for $N$ Majorana fermions, realizing the $\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{L}\times\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{R}$ lattice chiral symmetry. We also construct an exact lattice model for the Schwinger model and numerically reproduce the mass gap $e/\sqrt{\pi}$.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Heng Shao, Nikita Sopenko

item.title: An Atlas of Classical Pyrochlore Spin Liquids
item.description: arXiv:2411.03547v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Frustrated magnetism in the pyrochlore lattice magnet has proven to be a most fruitful setting for the experimental and theoretical search for spin liquids. Besides the canonical case of spin ice, recent works have identified a variety of new classical and quantum spin liquids engendered by the generic nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian for that lattice. However, a general framework for the thorough and systematic classification and characterization of these exotic states of matter has been lacking, as has an exhaustive list of all possible spin liquids that this model can support and, perhaps most interesting, what is the corresponding structure of their emergent field theory description. In this work, we develop such a theoretical framework to identify the interaction parameters stabilizing different classical spin liquids and derive their corresponding effective generalized Gauss's laws at low temperatures. Combining this with Monte Carlo simulations, we systematically identify all classical spin liquids for the general nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian on the pyrochlore lattice. In doing so, we uncover new spin liquid models with exotic forms of generalized Gauss's law and multipole conservation laws. Our approach allows us to compile an atlas of all spin liquids realized in the phase diagram, providing a global picture of their mutual connections in parameter space and transitions between them. Our work will inform future theoretical and experimental studies of classical and quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice and help rationalize the exotic properties of pyrochlore magnets.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Lozano-G\'omez, Owen Benton, Michel J. P. Gingras, Han Yan

item.title: Spectroscopic Evidence of Competing Diagonal Spin Interactions and Spin Disproportionation in the Bilayer Nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
item.description: arXiv:2602.05365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A comprehensive spectroscopic map of the electronic, magnetic, and lattice excitations is presented for the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ using Raman scattering at ambient pressure. Upon entering the spin density wave state below 153 K, the $A_{1g}$ channel exhibits an abrupt electronic spectral gap with a clear isosbestic point. In contrast, the $B_{1g}$ and $B_{2g}$ channels are dominated by pronounced two-magnon (2M) excitations, representing a signature of incipient Mottness. These 2M signals in both channels constitute evidence for two distinct in-plane spin exchange interactions along the Ni-O bonding and its diagonal directions. Calculations based on the spin wave theory further reveal that the 2M mode in the $B_{2g}$ channel arises from the competition between two bond-diagonal antiferromagnetic interactions mediated by nickel $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals. Furthermore, emergent low-energy 2M excitations below 10 meV are found to originate from distinct, weaker spin moments, supporting spin disproportionation. Simultaneously, an anomalous softening of $B_{1g}$ phonons from 280 down to 4.5 K is uncovered, suggesting the presence of an incipient lattice instability leading to checkerboard-type breathing modulations. Collectively, these findings identify a ground state of the bilayer nickelate characterized by competing bond-diagonal interactions, spin disproportionation, and an incipient lattice instability, establishing key ingredients for understanding the mechanism of nickelate superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Dong-Hyeon Gim, Dirk Wulferding, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Meng Wang, Kee Hoon Kim

item.title: Direction-selective intertwined charge, orbital, and lattice orders under uniaxial strain in hole-doped manganite: La0.75Ca0.25MnO3
item.description: arXiv:2605.27979v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The complex interplay of charge, spin, orbital, and lattice degrees of freedom governs emergent phases in quantum materials, making strain a powerful control parameter. Recent advances in free-standing layer techniques have enabled extreme strains of nearly 8%, opening access to novel and often unexpected electronic and magnetic phases. Here, using a density functional theory approach, we investigate the effect of direction-selective uniaxial strain on the prototypical Jahn-Teller system La1-xCaxMnO3 (x = 0.25). We find that different strain directions stabilize qualitatively distinct structural, charge, and orbital responses, rather than merely different strengths of the same phase. In particular, extreme uniaxial strain selectively induces cooperative Jahn-Teller, breathing-like, and site-selective modulations, thereby enabling previously inaccessible intertwined orders in manganites. These results establish direction-selective uniaxial strain as a powerful and selective route for engineering emergent phases in quantum materials.
item.dc:creator: Ju Hyeon Lee, Beom Hyun Kim, Bongjae Kim

item.title: Theory of Kondo hybridization wave in Kondo lattice
item.description: arXiv:2609.08467v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy experiments have discovered emergent spatially modulated Kondo hybridization wave (KHW) order in the heavy fermion superconductor UTe$_2$ and the artificial Kondo lattice system 1T/1H-TaS$_2$, challenging the conventional paradigm of spatially uniform Kondo hybridization in heavy fermion physics. Here, we develop a microscopic theory for KHW order based on the canonical square-lattice Kondo lattice model within the large-$N$ fermionic mean-field approximation. We systematically identify stable modulated KHW phases and establish their ground-state phase diagram. The prominent $\boldsymbol{Q}=(0,\pi)$ KHW phase yields uniaxial stripe modulation of the Kondo hybridization gap, which faithfully reproduces the spatial modulation pattern observed in UTe$_2$. Moreover, its inherent unit-cell-doubling modulation precisely accounts for the spectroscopic features measured in 1T/1H-TaS$_2$. We further predict a characteristic in-plane conductivity anisotropy that serves as a definitive transport fingerprint to discriminate KHW states with distinct ordering wavevectors. Our work provides a microscopic foundation for the newly observed KHW order and establishes a unified theoretical framework for understanding emergent modulated hybridization phenomena in heavy fermion materials.
item.dc:creator: Yin Zhong

item.title: Heavy-fermion hybridization waves from Dirac spinons near a Kondo-breakdown quantum phase transition
item.description: arXiv:2610.07146v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the recent observation of spatially modulated screening in different paramagnetic heavy-fermion materials, we propose a theoretical mechanism for the emergence of such hybridization waves in frustrated Kondo lattices with no magnetic order. By applying both a parton mean-field theory and a perturbative calculation to a minimal Kondo-Heisenberg lattice model, we demonstrate that a heavy Fermi liquid can naturally develop hybridization waves when it approaches a quantum phase transition where Kondo screening breaks down and the local magnetic moments form a Dirac spin liquid. We relate the strength of this mechanism to a kinematic condition on the electronic and spinon band structures and show that the spatial periodicity of the ensuing hybridization wave is controlled by momenta $\vec{Q}$ that connect the Dirac nodes in the spinon dispersion to low-energy portions of the electronic band structure.
item.dc:creator: Pedro M. C\^onsoli, Matthias Vojta, Onur Erten

item.title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25046v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting ($\mathrm{SC}_1$), and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Hao Wen, Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

item.title: Categorical classification of non-Fermi liquids in 2+1 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A defining feature of non-Fermi liquids is a lack of the quasiparticle peak on the Fermi surface in the spectral function, which is usually realized by coupling a finite density of fermions with critical collective fluctuations. However, these features of the two- and three-point vertex functions are qualitatively the same across many non-Fermi liquids, which has made it difficult to classify them beyond the definition by negation. We point out that the four-point function in the pairing channel contains rich information that positively differentiates distinct types of non-Fermi liquids. Using the generalized notion of fixed points that captures scale-dependent universal pairing interaction, we provide a non-perturbative classification of 2+1-dimensional non-Fermi liquids. In the large Fermi momentum limit with fixed dimensionless couplings, metals coupled with long-wavelength critical fluctuations are classified into seven superuniversality classes. Each of them exhibits a unique phase diagram in the space of temperature and bare four-fermion coupling. The present work generalizes the earlier perturbative classification to strongly interacting non-Fermi liquids by leveraging kinematic constraints.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Kukreja, Dawson M. Willerton, Sung-Sik Lee

item.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
item.description: arXiv:2610.38704v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The chiral central charge $c$ measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase and fixes the heat current along its edge. It has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that a calibrated combination of directional edge absorption weights determines $c$. A modulation of the edge couplings that travels along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra, and a static change of the same couplings measures the unknown probe normalization. Two harmonics then cancel the dependence on the edge state, so the estimator returns $c$ in any state of the ideal edge theory. A ratio of line weights with and without a vison gives the conformal spin of the Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb model, exact calculations recover $c=1/2$ and $h_\sigma=1/16$ to $10^{-5}$ and give $c$ within about $1\%$ on 96 spins. Compiled into gate circuits on the physical spins of a square-lattice quantum simulator, the protocol returns $c$ within $5\%$ on 48 qubits. For stochastic gate errors it requires two-qubit error rates of $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Ghosh

item.title: Bootstrapping transport in the Drude-Kadanoff-Martin model
item.description: arXiv:2509.18255v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Drude-Kadanoff-Martin model is a simple low energy and long wavelength description of charge transport, parameterised by the current relaxation timescale $\tau$, charge diffusivity $D$ and charge compressibility $\chi$. We obtain sharp constraints on these parameters in terms of the microscopic energy and length scales of any underlying lattice model with local and bounded interactions. Our primary tools are upper bounds on the retarded Green's function for the charge density in such a setting. We first note that the Drude-Kadanoff-Martin model cannot pertain at microscopic energy scales because it is inconsistent with the exponential suppression of spectral weight at the highest frequencies in a lattice model. Secondly, under the assumption that the low energy dynamics is captured by the model, we obtain a lower bound on the collective mean free path $\ell \equiv \sqrt{\tau D}$. This bound is shown to imply a version of the Mott-Ioffe-Regel bound: systems with $\ell$ much shorter than the lattice length scale cannot have conventional Drude peaks, in the sense of being captured by the DKM model.
item.dc:creator: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Sean A. Hartnoll, Aditya Hebbar, Ruby Khondaker

item.title: Quantum Matrix-Element Estimators for Spin-Coupled Generalized Valence Bond (SCGVB) Wavefunctions
item.description: arXiv:2603.12045v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Valence-bond wavefunctions such as spin-coupled generalized valence bond (SCGVB) provide compact and chemically interpretable descriptions of strong correlation, but their nonorthogonal determinant structure makes quantum evaluation of overlaps and Hamiltonian matrix elements difficult. Here we introduce an ancilla-free, measurement-driven framework that reformulates these quantities as vacuum expectation values of Pauli-string operators, enabling evaluation with shallow circuits, local Clifford rotations, and computational-basis measurements, without controlled operations. We validate the method for H$_4$ along a dissociation pathway and for a 70-determinant C$_2$ active-valence benchmark. The reconstructed matrices agree with the classical L{\"o}wdin-based reference, while Chirgwin-Coulson weights remain chemically consistent. These results establish the proposed estimators as a low-depth, circuit-compatible formulation for evaluating SCGVB matrix elements, while making no claim of quantum computational advantage.
item.dc:creator: Bruna Bruna G. M. Ara\'ujo

item.title: Loss of altermagnetic order and smooth restoration of Kramers' spin degeneracy with increasing temperature in CrSb and MnTe
item.description: arXiv:2603.15035v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe how thermally induced spin fluctuations modify the electronic structures of two prototypical altermagnets, CrSb and MnTe, via application of the disordered local moment picture. For both materials, our self-consistent, ab initio calculations demonstrate that local magnetic moments persist on Cr and Mn atoms in their paramagnetic states, necessitating a spin-polarised description of the electronic structure even above the N\'eel temperature, $T_\mathrm{N}$. Moreover, Kramers' spin degeneracy, which is broken for both materials in their altermagnetic ground states, is shown to be smoothly restored - on the average - as the local moments thermally disorder. In metallic CrSb, this occurs at temperatures well below $T_\mathrm{N}$ and the signature effects of its altermagnetism are lost as the magnetic disorder induces heavy smearing of strongly dispersive electronic states around the Fermi energy. By contrast, in semiconducting MnTe, with its band gap largely unaffected by magnetic disorder, the spin degeneracy only returns at temperatures close to and above $T_\mathrm{N}$. We quantify the temperature dependence of the altermagnetic order parameter and the underlying electronic structures of both materials, with implications for their spin transport and spectroscopic properties.
item.dc:creator: Christopher D. Woodgate, Nabil Menai, Arthur Ernst, Julie B. Staunton

item.title: Deterministic Hypergraph SYK: Melonic Dominance and Maximal Chaos Without Disorder Averaging
item.description: arXiv:2609.19255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the leading melonic structure of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model can be realized by a single sparse Majorana Hamiltonian, without disorder averaging. In our deterministic hypergraph SYK model (hSYK), $N$ Majorana fermions interact through $O(dN)$ terms with uniform couplings, arranged on a fixed $q$-uniform, $d$-regular hypergraph. If the hypergraph is linear, has few short cycles, and is a spectral expander, then at large $d$ the two-point function obeys the melonic Schwinger-Dyson equation site by site. The leading thermodynamics are therefore those of SYK, and at leading order in $1/d$ every bilocal fluctuation other than the Schwarzian is gapped. The four-point ladder splits into scrambling modes labeled by eigenvalues of the site adjacency operator. At strong coupling, the uniform mode is maximally chaotic, and a non-uniform mode grows only if its eigenvalue exceeds $1/(q-1)$. Exact diagonalization of single instances with $N\le24$ agrees with the melonic two-point function and thermodynamics more closely than dense SYK of the same size, shows Wigner-Dyson level statistics, and reproduces the predicted mode structure of out-of-time-order correlators. Numerically, random linear hypergraphs typically satisfy these conditions, and for $d>q$ also avoid emergent symmetries. The model is a natural candidate for quantum simulation.
item.dc:creator: Shiroman Prakash

item.title: Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2610.33808v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It was experimentally observed that Wigner-crystal and chiral superconducting phases occur adjacent to each other in rhombohedral graphene. In this Letter, we explore electronic correlations underlying the two phases and identify the pairing mechanism of chiral superconductivity. Exchange correlations play an essential role in both phases. First, we use self-consistent Hartree-Fock calculations to identify a Wigner-crystal state. Second, to investigate the pairing mechanism, we go beyond charge screening and construct a particle-hole-renormalized interaction through the coupled parquet and Bethe-Salpeter equations. This interaction incorporates exchange correlations while preserving crossing symmetry. Within this framework, we find that electronic correlations in the quarter metal are strongly enhanced near the crystal phase boundary, generating an effective attraction that favors superconducting pairing. Consequently, chiral superconductivity (CSC) emerges in a narrow sliver adjacent to the crystal. Furthermore, we identify the winding number of the superconducting order parameter as $-3$, indicating its $f$-wave nature. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.
item.dc:creator: Ke Wang

item.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
item.description: arXiv:2611.03207v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Dey, Abel Carreras, Siddhartha Patra
